mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Viano 2.2 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Viano 2.2 CDI engine replacement typically costs between £1,200 and £3,000 depending on engine code (OM611, OM646 or OM651), condition type, and whether fitting is included. Rebuilt OM611 (W638, 1996-2003): £1,200-£1,800 supply only. Rebuilt OM646 (W639, 2003-2010): £1,400-£2,500 supply only. Rebuilt OM651 (W639 facelift, 2010-2014): £1,800-£3,000 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £450-£1,600 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £400-£800 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Mercedes Viano 2.2 CDI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common failure depends on the engine generation. On the OM646 (2003-2010), timing chain tensioner failure (A6460500307) is the dominant issue, causing rattle on cold start and potential catastrophic engine failure. OM611 (W638, 1996-2003): injector pump seal failure - diesel in oil. OM646 (W639, 2003-2010): timing chain tensioner failure - cold start rattle. OM651 (W639 facelift, 2010-2014): timing chain stretch and fuel pump failure. Camshaft encoder wheel failure can cause stalling and rough starts across all variants.

mainEntity.name: Is the OM646 engine in the Viano 2.2 CDI reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM646 is fundamentally a strong engine - many examples exceed 200,000-250,000 miles - but it has one critical weakness: the timing chain tensioner. Timing chain tensioner failure is predictable between 80k-140k miles. Cold start rattle is the earliest warning sign. Updated dual-spring tensioner (A6460502201) is the permanent fix. Catch it early - preventative chain replacement costs £768-£1,280 at a specialist. Once the chain slips, piston-valve contact means a full replacement engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Viano 2.2 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.2 CDI timing chain typically shows warning signs before complete failure. Rattling or clanking noise on cold start - the earliest warning sign. Rattle that lasts more than 2-3 seconds indicates significant chain stretch. Check engine light with cam/crank correlation codes (P0016/P0017). If ignored, the chain can jump teeth and destroy the engine. Metallic swarf in engine oil indicates chain guides wearing away.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my Viano 2.2 CDI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner on OM646, injector pump seals on OM611, sensors). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. OM646 timing chain tensioner replacement: £768-£1,280 - do this at first sign of rattle. OM611 injector pump seal replacement: £350-£600 - do this immediately if oil level rises. Camshaft sensor & encoder wheel: £250-£450 - resolves stalling and rough starts. Full OM646 rebuild: £1,800-£2,800 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Full OM651 rebuild: £2,400-£3,500 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Given Viano 2.2 CDI values (£3,000-£10,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my Viano 2.2 CDI has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block near the starter motor. W638 Viano (1996-2003): OM611. W639 Viano (2003-2010): OM646 (109 CDI, 111 CDI, 115 CDI). W639 facelift Viano (2010-2014): OM651 (113 CDI, 116 CDI). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used Viano 2.2 CDI engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a Viano 2.2 CDI. The W639 subframe geometry and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Subframe must be lowered - not a driveway job. 9G-Tronic or 6-speed manual alignment requires specialist knowledge. Immobiliser and injector coding must be programmed. Specialist supply & fit costs £400-£800 - worth every penny.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz Viano 2.2 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Benz Viano 2.2 CDI powered the vast majority of UK Viano sales across two generations - the W638 (1996-2003) with the OM611 engine, and the W639 (2003-2014) with the OM646 and later OM651 engines. This 2.2-litre common-rail diesel family defined the Viano's reputation as a robust, economical people carrier, though each generation brought distinct reliability challenges.

milestones.description: W638 Viano launched with OM611 2.2L common-rail diesel, 90-125hp, Bosch injection system
W639 Viano launched with OM646 2.2L diesel (modified OM611), 109-150hp, Euro III emissions
OM646 gains Euro IV emissions compliance with EGR cooler and DPF
W639 facelift introduces OM651 2.2L diesel with 136-163hp, twin-turbo on higher-output variants
Viano production ends, replaced by Mercedes V-Class

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every 2.2 CDI engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz Viano is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points from real owner experience.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz Viano 2.2 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Viano 2.2 CDI - whether OM611, OM646 or OM651 - is the backbone of UK Viano diesel ownership. Each engine family has distinct, well-documented failure patterns. The OM646 timing chain tensioner dominates replacement demand, while OM611 injector pump seal failure and OM651 chain stretch also drive significant repair enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common Viano 2.2 CDI engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM646 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Viano 2.2 CDI Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The original OM646 timing chain tensioner (OEM A6460500307) fails to maintain adequate oil pressure, allowing the single-row timing chain to slacken. This produces a characteristic rattle on cold start and, if ignored, can lead to timing correlation faults and chain skip - with catastrophic piston-valve contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, updated dual-spring tensioner (A6460502201), guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles; only viable if caught before chain slip

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit reconditioned OM646 with upgraded tensioner, reinforced guide rails, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles; the definitive fix for engines with timing damage or skipped chains

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W639 Viano 2.2 CDI is worth £3,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage - the full replacement cost of £1,800-£2,800 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £3,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: If you hear chain rattle on cold start or have camshaft correlation fault codes (P0016/P0017), act immediately. Preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£768-£1,280) is far cheaper than a full engine replacement. On a Viano worth £3,000-£6,000, once the chain has slipped and damaged valves, replacement is usually the correct financial decision.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM646 engine prices for your Mercedes Viano 2.2 CDI

problems.h4: OM611 Injector Pump Seal Failure - Why the W638 Viano 2.2 CDI Has Diesel in the Oil
problems.rootCause: The injector pump seal fails internally, allowing diesel fuel to leak into the engine oil sump. The rising oil level and thinned, fuel-diluted oil causes rapid bearing wear, low oil pressure, and eventual catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of injector pump seals, full oil and filter change (multiple flushes may be required)
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix if caught before bearing damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit reconditioned engine with new seals, pump, and bearings
repairOptions.longevity: Required if engine has run with fuel-diluted oil for extended period

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W638 Viano 2.2 CDI is worth £1,500-£4,000 - the full replacement cost of £1,400-£2,200 often approaches or exceeds vehicle value. Evaluate carefully.
problems.recommendation: Check your dipstick regularly - if the oil level rises between services or smells strongly of diesel, stop driving immediately. Early detection means a £350-£600 specialist repair. Ignoring it will destroy the bottom end and require a full replacement engine. On an older W638 Viano, replacement often exceeds the vehicle's value.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM611 Mercedes Viano 2.2 CDI replacement engines

problems.group: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch & Fuel Pump Failure
problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch & Fuel Pump Failure - Facelift Viano 2.2 CDI Concerns
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Viano 113 CDI, 116 CDI, 2.2 CDI facelift (2010-2014, OM651)
problems.rootCause: The OM651 uses a simplex roller timing chain. A faulty chain tensioner can cause premature chain elongation, producing rattling on cold start and potential engine damage. Fuel pump failure (TSB 07.01.15) can also occur without warning on high-mileage examples.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides - engine-out job on OM651
Supply & fit reconditioned OM651 with new timing components and upgraded tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped or fuel pump failure has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical facelift W639 Viano 2.2 CDI (2010-2014) is worth £4,000-£10,000 - the full replacement cost of £2,400-£3,500 is modest relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine a sound investment for well-maintained examples.
problems.recommendation: The OM651 timing chain stretch is a known weakness - if you hear rattling on cold start, have it inspected immediately. Engine-out replacement is technically complex, so choose a specialist who has done this job before. Post-2013 examples have improved chain components, but early OM651 engines (2010-2012) are most vulnerable.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes Viano 2.2 CDI engine prices

problems.group: Viano 2.2 CDI Camshaft Encoder Wheel & EGR Cooler Issues
problems.h4: Viano 2.2 CDI Camshaft Encoder Wheel & EGR Cooler Issues - Emissions and Starting Faults
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Viano 2.2 CDI (OM646, OM651, all years)
problems.rootCause: The camshaft encoder wheel can fail, causing rough starts, stalling at idle, and check engine lights. EGR cooler carbon lock (Euro IV OM646 engines, 2006-2010) causes restricted exhaust flow, power loss and limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace camshaft position sensor and encoder wheel, clear fault codes
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-120k miles; resolves stalling and starting issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler, clean EGR valve, perform DPF regeneration
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles; resolves loss of power and limp mode

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit reconditioned OM646/OM651 with new sensors and EGR components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required for persistent emissions failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a Viano 2.2 CDI worth £3,000-£10,000, sensor replacement at £250-£450 is excellent value. EGR cooler replacement at £500-£800 is also justified. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: If your Viano 2.2 CDI stalls at idle or has rough starts, have the camshaft sensor and encoder wheel checked first - the encoder wheel is a known weak point. For Euro IV OM646 engines (2006-2010) used primarily for short trips, the EGR cooler will block again; consider a professional EGR delete (where MOT-legal) or switch to a specialist who can fit a modified cooling setup.
